package_info.package_name: SplitLoader (malicious npm package, also distributed as part of DeTankWar game)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is distributed as part of a social engineering campaign, masquerading as coding test assignments or a game, and is designed to deliver custom malware loaders (SplitLoader) that enable further payload execution, data theft, and facilitate cyberespionage and ransomware deployment.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads an encrypted payload from disk, decrypts it using a key from an environment variable, writes the decrypted payload to disk, and executes it as a new process, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code decrypts and executes a hidden payload at import-time, which is a common malware loader technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not decrypt and execute hidden binaries during import; legitimate packages should not execute arbitrary code on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may unpack and run binaries, but not in the context of a coding test or game package.
key_indicators: Use of environment variables for decryption keys

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads sensitive files from the victim's filesystem and exfiltrates them to a remote command-and-control server via HTTPS POST, enabling data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates local files to an external server, which is a hallmark of espionage malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access arbitrary user files or transmit them to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud backup tools may upload files, but only with user consent and to trusted domains.
key_indicators: Access to user files without consent
Network exfiltration to hardcoded C2 domains

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious npm package (SplitLoader or DeTankWar) under the guise of a coding test or game.
Malicious code in the package decrypts and executes an embedded payload (malware loader).
The executed payload (malware loader) accesses sensitive files and exfiltrates data to a remote C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, espionage, or further malware deployment

behavioral_signatures: Decryption and execution of embedded payloads at import-time
Access to sensitive user files by npm packages
Network connections to untrusted or hardcoded C2 domains
file_indicators: Presence of payload.enc or similar encrypted payload files in npm package
Unexpected binaries written and executed (e.g., payload.exe) during package use
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate function
Connections to known malicious C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for code that decrypts and executes hidden payloads, especially if triggered at import-time. Flag packages that access user files or environment variables and initiate outbound network connections to untrusted domains. Look for the presence of encrypted payload files and unexpected binary execution within package directories.
